sections.h2: How is Coon Rapids organized on the map?
sections.html:
Coon Rapids sits north of Minneapolis and ranks second in size among Anoka County cities. Its 22.61 square miles of land lie about 863 feet up, and the 2025 Census estimate counts 64,193 residents.

The Mississippi River runs along the city, and Cenaiko Lake and Crooked Lake lie within the boundaries. Two-thirds of Crooked Lake belongs to Coon Rapids, with the remaining third in Andover. U.S. Highway 10, Minnesota Highway 47 and Minnesota Highway 610 carry most of the traffic, and the BNSF mainline cuts through town. Coon Rapids Boulevard follows the old oxcart route and remains the main commercial corridor. A house a block from those roads draws a different crowd than one on a quiet street near a park, so the address shapes how a sale goes.

sections.h2: How did Coon Rapids grow from an oxcart route to a city of 64,000?
sections.html:
The name comes from Coon Creek, where settlers hunted raccoons in the 1800s. The Red River Ox Cart Trail was laid out in 1835 to link Minneapolis and Anoka, and early industry grew up beside it. One firm was the Anoka Pressed Brick and Terra Cotta Company, started by D. C. Dunham in 1881. Its clay pit, still called the Clay Hole, is a local landmark.

Work on the Coon Rapids Dam began in 1912 and finished in 1914, and the dam marks the northernmost navigable point on the Mississippi. The Hennepin County Park Board bought it in 1969, and it is now part of Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park. The place incorporated as a village in October 1952 and as a city in June 1959.

Growth after that was fast. The count was 14,931 in 1960, 30,505 in 1970, 52,978 in 1990 and 63,599 at the 2020 census. A city that more than tripled between 1960 and 1990 has many houses that are now several decades old, which matters when you think about roofs, windows and mechanical systems before listing.

sections.h2: Which jobs, schools and parks influence Coon Rapids home values?
sections.html:
Health care, schools and manufacturing anchor the local job base. The city's 2014 financial report named these employers among its largest.

  • Mercy Health, part of Allina Health, with 1,860 employees.
  • Independent School District 11, with 1,238.
  • Mary T, Inc., a health care and housing provider, with 1,120.
  • RMS Company, a medical device maker, with 672, followed by Honeywell Aerospace with 600 and Anoka-Ramsey Community College with 403.

Anoka-Hennepin District 11 runs the public schools. Coon Rapids High School is projected at about 1,935 students for 2025-26, and the middle schools are Coon Rapids Middle and Northdale Middle. Seven elementary schools serve the city: Adams, Eisenhower, Hamilton, Hoover, Mississippi, Morris Bye and Sand Creek. Charter options include Paladin Career and Technical High School and Northwest Passage High School.

Bunker Hills Regional Park, with its Bunker Beach water park, and Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park both lie inside the city limits.

sections.html:
Three of every four Coon Rapids households own, and the typical owner-occupied home is valued near $306,000. The table shows the headline numbers.

sections.h2: Which Coon Rapids rental and vacancy rules matter when you sell?
sections.html:
Coon Rapids regulates rentals and empty houses more closely than many suburbs, and the rules can affect both your timeline and what a buyer may do with the property.

  • Every rental, single-family homes included, must hold a city license before tenants move in. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks and includes a background check for each owner, a training certificate and a passed inspection.
  • Licenses renew every year, and starting in 2026 a late renewal brings a late fee. Inspections run on a 1, 2 or 3 year cycle based on results.
  • City Code 12-904 prohibits Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals, so a buyer cannot plan on that use.
  • A vacant house needs a vacant property permit. You submit the application with the fee, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to book a one-hour inspection.

If renters occupy the house, phone the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 first. That call tells you where your license and inspection cycle stand.

sections.h2: Which Coon Rapids repairs call for a permit first?
sections.html:
Most of them do. The city lists windows, siding, roofing, electrical and plumbing work, drywall, demolition, framing, additions, garages, driveways, steps and decks as projects that need building permits, and some jobs also require a licensed contractor.

Unpermitted work can draw questions once a buyer's inspector looks at the house. Call the Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 before you hire anyone. If the house needs more work than you want to take on, a sale to a buyer who handles repairs after closing is an alternative, though the price will reflect the work still to do.

sections.h2: What does Anoka County require to record a Coon Rapids deed?
sections.html:
The Anoka County Recorder accepts the deed for filing. State deed tax runs 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, so a $305,800 price carries roughly $1,009.

  • Sales of $3,000 or under pay a flat $1.65.
  • An agricultural conservation fee of $5 applies to transfer documents.
  • When an eCRV applies, its filing number is written on the deed.
  • The deed names the buyer and the address for tax statements.
  • Anoka County will not record a transfer while delinquent tax remains unpaid.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or the approved well statement printed on the deed.

Most Anoka County property is abstract property, so the county advises a thorough title search before a sale. Recording questions go to 763-323-5400 at the Government Center in Anoka. Statute 513.55 adds a duty to hand the buyer a written list of known material problems before signing.

sections.h2: How is property tax paid when a Coon Rapids house sells?
sections.html:
Anoka County Property Records and Taxation collects the tax, and the county's property access site shows what is owed by parcel number or address. Call 763-323-5400 for the unpaid balance and the next due date. Your closing agent can explain the proration.

If you still owe tax before the sale, the choices are these. Online payment through PayAnokaCounty adds 2.6 percent for cards and Apple or Google Pay, or $3.50 for eCheck. A mailed check counts as on time only with a postmark dated by the due date. Paper checks paid at the Government Center counter, where weekday hours end at 4:30 p.m., carry no fee. The county's free Direct Payment Program pulls the amount from a bank account on the due date.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Coon Rapids house?
sections.html:
Three routes exist here: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or an offer from a cash buyer. The best match depends on repairs, the calendar and who lives in the house now.

A listing gives the most buyer exposure and suits a house in solid shape. A direct cash sale trades some price for speed and fewer conditions, which can help with a vacant house, a former rental that needs inspection work, or deferred repairs. Whichever you pick, pull together the rental license status, any open permits, the well disclosure and the tax balance first, since every buyer asks for them.

faqs.q: Is it possible to sell a Coon Rapids house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes, after you check the rental license. The city requires every rental, including single-family homes, to be licensed and inspected, so call the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 to confirm where your license and inspection cycle stand.

faqs.q: Can a Coon Rapids buyer use the house for Airbnb stays?
faqs.a: No. City Code 12-904 bans Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals in Coon Rapids, so a buyer with that plan cannot count on it.

faqs.q: What is the state deed tax on a Coon Rapids sale?
faqs.a: It is 0.33 percent of net consideration, or $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less. On a $305,800 sale that is about $1,009. Anoka County adds a $5 conservation fee, and a well disclosure certificate costs $54 unless the approved well statement appears on the deed.

faqs.q: Does fixing up a Coon Rapids house before a sale require a permit?
faqs.a: For most projects, yes. Windows, siding, roofing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, decks, driveways and additions all need building permits. The Inspections Division, at 763-767-6476, can say whether a particular job is covered.

faqs.q: How does the city treat a vacant house in Coon Rapids?
faqs.a: It requires a vacant property permit. Submit the application and fee at City Hall, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to schedule the one-hour inspection. Property Maintenance at 763-767-6470 takes complaints about empty properties.
